aphids.name: Aphids
prevent: Avoid excessive nitrogen that encourages soft growth.
organic: Use a strong water spray on colonies.
Use insecticidal soap or horticultural oil only as labelled.
chemical: Use only a locally approved aphid product if monitoring shows treatment is necessary.
Protect flowering plants and pollinators; follow the label.
aphids.field_note: Clusters on new growth and sticky honeydew are useful clues, but several insects can look similar in a single photo.
aphids.source: Verify with local extension guidance and the product label.

fall armyworm.name: Fall armyworm
prevent: Scout whorls and leaf surfaces early.
Remove volunteer plants and crop residue where appropriate.
Use crop rotation and field sanitation.
organic: Use approved biological products based on Bt or beneficial organisms.
Support natural enemies by avoiding unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays.
chemical: Use an approved product only after confirming the pest and local threshold.
Rotate modes of action to reduce resistance risk.
fall armyworm.field_note: Look for window-pane feeding and frass deep in the plant whorl; confirm before treatment.
fall armyworm.source: Verify with local crop protection guidance and the product label.

beet armyworm.name: Beet armyworm
prevent: Scout young leaves and plant margins.
Use physical barriers for small plots.
organic: Remove egg masses and larvae by hand in small areas.
Use approved microbial controls where suitable.
chemical: Choose only a locally registered option and follow its label.
Avoid repeated use of the same mode of action.
beet armyworm.field_note: Larval colour varies, so feeding pattern and crop context matter as much as appearance.
beet armyworm.source: Verify with local crop protection guidance and the product label.

caterpillar.name: Caterpillar-type pest
prevent: Scout leaves and growing points early in the morning.
Check leaf undersides and look for frass, webbing, or fresh chewing damage.
Remove weeds and crop residue that can shelter larvae.
organic: Hand-pick visible larvae and egg masses where practical.
Use an approved Bt-based biological control on young caterpillars, following the local label.
Protect birds, parasitoids, and other natural enemies by avoiding unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays.
chemical: Do not choose a product from this low-confidence category alone; confirm the species and crop first.
If treatment is justified, use only a locally registered product, follow its label, and rotate modes of action to reduce resistance.
caterpillar.field_note: The image suggests a caterpillar-like pest category, but species-level identification is uncertain. Look for the crop, feeding pattern, frass, and body markings before treatment.
caterpillar.source: General integrated-pest-management guidance; verify with local agricultural extension advice and the product label.

unknown.name: Uncertain field observation
prevent: Retake the photo in natural light.
Include the insect and the damage pattern.
Capture the underside of leaves if possible.
organic: Avoid treatment until the pest is confirmed.
Isolate heavily affected plant material where practical.
chemical: Do not apply chemical control from an uncertain prediction.
Ask a local agricultural expert for confirmation.
unknown.field_note: The safest recommendation when confidence is low is better evidence, not stronger treatment.
